# WinRM Kerberos kinit fix

Status: complete. Added the `ansible_winrm_kinit_args` option, parsed its arguments with `shlex.split`, and shared the same command tokens between subprocess and pexpect. Explicit arguments override the default delegation flag; absent arguments retain it. Documented the option and added tests for both execution paths, precedence, argument parsing, and distinct credential caches per attempt.

Verification: `python -m pytest test/units/plugins/connection/test_winrm.py -q` (35 passed); `git diff --check` passed.

     ansible_winrm_kinit_mode: managed/manual (manual means Ansible will not obtain a ticket)
     ansible_winrm_kinit_cmd: the kinit binary to use to obtain a Kerberos ticket (default to kinit)
+    ansible_winrm_kinit_args: arguments to pass to the kinit binary (replaces default arguments, including the delegation flag)
     ansible_winrm_service: overrides the SPN prefix that is used, the default is ``HTTP`` and should rarely ever need changing
     ansible_winrm_kerberos_delegation: allows the credentials to traverse multiple hops
     ansible_winrm_kerberos_hostname_override: the hostname to be used for the kerberos exchange
@@ -399,6 +400,10 @@ Automatic ticket management requires a standard ``kinit`` binary on the control
 host system path. To specify a different location or binary name, set the
 ``ansible_winrm_kinit_cmd`` hostvar to the fully qualified path to a MIT krbv5
 ``kinit``-compatible binary.
+If the binary needs extra arguments, set ``ansible_winrm_kinit_args`` to a
+space-separated string, for example ``-krb -init``. Arguments supplied this way
+replace the default ``-f`` flag used for Kerberos delegation, so include it
+explicitly if the binary requires it.
